events.name: Blind Tom No. 2 and Rev. Dr. Manley at Bainbridge Street Church (broadside, April 27, 1893)
events.location: Bainbridge Street Church, Bainbridge Street below Twelfth, Philadelphia
events.description: Printed broadside (handbill): 'Last opportunity to see and hear, The Blind Musician.' With an engraved portrait. 'Blind Tom No. 2. The wonderful Piano and Organ player, is in the city with Dr. Manley, the Missionary Secretary, from Knoxvill[e] Tennessee. Rev. Manley is a noted Gospel Singer. He is called the Black Sankey. He will both amuse and please you. These two natural born Musicians will perform and sing at Bainbridge Street Church, Bainbridge Street below Twelfth. Thursday Eve. April 27th. ’93. On this occasion some of the best local talent will appear.' Admission: general 25 cents, reserved seat 35 cents, children 15 cents. 'Proceed[s] for the benefit of said Church. Rev. W. H. Coffey, Pastor.' Printed by Cooper, Parker and Purnell, Printers, 1110 Lombard St., Phila. The performer is not named on the bill. Dr. Manley (of Knoxville) is out of town and is in the text only. Source: Dorsey Collection, Box 25 (SB-3); photograph supplied by Michiko Quinones, 2026-11-23.
attendees: pastor, Bainbridge Street Church (Rev.); the concert was for the benefit of his church
